title: LSP Time Off: plain-PHP + MySQL on cPanel, Google Calendars kept as a read-only mirror
lens: OPERATIONS-FIRST: the smallest thing that can be uploaded to cPanel and run for ten years with one part-time maintainer. Every choice below was made by asking "what breaks in year six, and who fixes it at 9pm?" Boring technology, no build step, no package manager on the server, one code folder that is disposable and one data folder that is precious.
stack:
LANGUAGE/RUNTIME: PHP 8.x through cPanel MultiPHP Manager. Pick the newest 8.x that MultiPHP offers today (ea-php84 on a current Liquid Web cPanel; ea-php83 if 84 is absent). Code is written to run unchanged on 8.2 through 8.5 (declare(strict_types=1), DateTimeImmutable, PDO, no dynamic properties, no deprecated calls), because over ten years you will bump the MultiPHP selection three or four times and the app must not care. Required extensions, all in the default EasyApache 4 PHP profile: pdo_mysql, curl, openssl, json, mbstring, session, zlib. setup.php checks for each and refuses to continue if one is missing.

FRAMEWORK: none. One PHP file per screen (index.php, requests.php, request.php, ...) with a shared lib/bootstrap.php (session, PDO, CSRF, auth, error handler) and lib/layout.php (header/nav/footer). No router, no .htaccess rewrites, so nothing depends on Apache module quirks; URLs are simply https://pto.lightsaberpromotions.com/requests.php. This matches how Chris already writes his XAMPP tools, which matters more for a ten-year horizon than any framework benefit. Rejected: Laravel/Symfony/Slim (Composer, vendor/ directory, upgrade treadmill that outpaces a part-time maintainer); Node/Express (not on cPanel by default); Docker (not on cPanel).

DATABASE: the MySQL/MariaDB that cPanel already runs (MariaDB 10.6 or MySQL 8 on Liquid Web). One database, one user, created in the MySQL Database Wizard; managed with the phpMyAdmin that is already in cPanel; included in the Liquid Web/cPanel account backups automatically. All SQL is plain InnoDB/utf8mb4 with no vendor-specific features (TEXT instead of the JSON type, no generated columns) so it runs identically on MariaDB and MySQL. Considered SQLite (single file in pto_data, zero DB setup) and rejected only because Chris explicitly wants a real database with a GUI, and MySQL costs nothing extra on cPanel.

FRONT-END: server-rendered HTML, one hand-written CSS file (~250 lines, responsive so the office manager can enter a request from a phone), one vanilla JS file (~120 lines: end-date defaults to start-date, live balance preview via fetch, confirm-on-delete). Native <input type="date">. No CDN links, no CSS framework, no bundler: nothing external that can disappear in year eight.

GOOGLE CALENDAR: raw Calendar API v3 over curl with a service-account JWT (RS256 via openssl_sign, RFC 7523). About 180 lines in lib/calendar.php. Rejected google/apiclient (Composer, ~100 packages, breaks on PHP upgrades, 30 MB for five calendars).

Total code: roughly 2,500 lines of PHP, all readable by a PHP-experienced maintainer in an afternoon.
hosting_fit:
What must exist on the Liquid Web cPanel account (one-time, about 45 minutes, all through the cPanel web UI, no SSH):

1. cPanel > Domains > Create a New Domain: pto.lightsaberpromotions.com, UNCHECK "share document root", set Document Root to /home/<cpuser>/pto_web. A subdomain rather than /pto/ under the main site so the main site's .htaccess, a WordPress install, or the ongoing rebrand/domain change can never clobber it; if the company domain changes later, create the new subdomain pointing at the same folder. Turn on "Force HTTPS Redirect" for it on the Domains page (no .htaccess needed). AutoSSL issues the certificate automatically within the hour (SSL/TLS Status > Run AutoSSL to hurry it).

2. cPanel > MultiPHP Manager: select pto.lightsaberpromotions.com, set PHP version ea-php84 (or the newest 8.x listed). cPanel > MultiPHP INI Editor for that domain: max_execution_time 90, memory_limit 128M, display_errors Off. Everything else default.

3. cPanel > MySQL Database Wizard: database <cpuser>_pto, user <cpuser>_pto, ALL PRIVILEGES, generate a long password. Write it into pto_data/config.php.

4. cPanel > File Manager: create /home/<cpuser>/pto_data (permissions 700) and upload config.php (copied from config.example.php) and google-service-account.json (permissions 600). Upload pto_web.zip to /home/<cpuser>/ and Extract; it creates /home/<cpuser>/pto_web/. pto_data is always the sibling folder of pto_web; bootstrap.php finds it with dirname(__DIR__, 2).'/pto_data' and dies with a plain-English message if it is missing. Same rule locally on XAMPP: C:\xampp\htdocs\pto_web and C:\xampp\htdocs\pto_data.

5. Browser: https://pto.lightsaberpromotions.com/setup.php. It checks PHP version and extensions, connects to the DB, runs lib/migrations/001_init.sql, creates the first admin user, seeds the five calendars rows, and then tells you to delete setup.php (it also refuses to run again once a user exists).

6. cPanel > Cron Jobs, three entries using the EA PHP binary (not /usr/local/bin/php, which may be a different version):
   */15 * * * *  /opt/cpanel/ea-php84/root/usr/bin/php -q /home/<cpuser>/pto_web/cron/sync.php >> /home/<cpuser>/pto_data/logs/cron.log 2>&1
   5 3 * * *     /opt/cpanel/ea-php84/root/usr/bin/php -q /home/<cpuser>/pto_web/cron/sync.php --all >> /home/<cpuser>/pto_data/logs/cron.log 2>&1
   20 3 * * *    /opt/cpanel/ea-php84/root/usr/bin/php -q /home/<cpuser>/pto_web/cron/backup.php >> /home/<cpuser>/pto_data/logs/cron.log 2>&1
   Each cron script prints its PHP version and the run summary into the log so a wrong-binary mistake is visible.

7. Google side (one time, Chris's Google Workspace account, about 20 minutes): console.cloud.google.com > New project "LSP Time Off" > Enable "Google Calendar API" > IAM > Service Accounts > create "lsp-pto-sync" > Keys > Add key (JSON) > download to pto_data/google-service-account.json. Then in Google Calendar, for each of the five calendars: Settings > Share with specific people > add the service account email with "Make changes to events". Paste the five calendar IDs (already in the Apps Script) into Admin > Calendars and click "Test connection". No domain-wide delegation, no OAuth consent screen, nothing expires.

8. Outbound HTTPS from the server to oauth2.googleapis.com and www.googleapis.com must be allowed (default on Liquid Web; if CSF blocks it, "Test connection" says so and the fix is a firewall allow entry via Liquid Web support).

Not required and not used: SSH, Composer, Node, git on the server, Redis, any PHP extension outside the default profile, any Apache module beyond mod_rewrite (used only by cPanel's own Force-HTTPS). pto_web/lib/, pto_web/cron/, pto_web/tests/ and pto_data/ each contain a .htaccess with "Require all denied"; a robots.txt disallows everything.

data_model:
-- MySQL 8 / MariaDB 10.3+, InnoDB, utf8mb4. All dates are DATE (no time-of-day anywhere); "today" is America/New_York, set in bootstrap.
-- Balances and cycles are NEVER stored; they are recomputed from employees + time_off + adjustments on every read (lib/balance.php), exactly as the sheet does.
-- Allotment tiers live in code (const in lib/balance.php: Vacation 0/5/10/15 at 0/1/5/10 years; PTO 0 under 1 year else 3), not in a table, because they change once a decade and a table invites accidental edits.

CREATE TABLE employees (
  id            INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
  last_name     VARCHAR(60)  NOT NULL,
  first_name    VARCHAR(60)  NOT NULL,          -- calendar title = CONCAT(last_name,', ',first_name) => "Walker, Rebecca - Vacation", byte-identical to today
  hire_date     DATE         NOT NULL,          -- anniversary anchor for the 12-month cycle
  birth_month   TINYINT UNSIGNED NULL,          -- 1-12
  birth_day     TINYINT UNSIGNED NULL,          -- 1-31; birth YEAR is deliberately not stored (sheet years are placeholders; only month/day is used)
  departed_on   DATE NULL,                      -- NULL = active. Departed employees: hidden from pickers, dashboard and api.php; all history and past calendar events kept; no birthday events generated; requests after departed_on flagged in UI
  notes         VARCHAR(255) NULL,
  created_at    DATETIME NOT NULL, updated_at DATETIME NOT NULL,
  UNIQUE KEY uq_emp_name (last_name, first_name)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;

CREATE TABLE time_off (                          -- the "Time Requested Off" sheet, minus the calculated columns
  id            INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
  employee_id   INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  kind          ENUM('PTO','Vacation') NOT NULL, -- casing normalized on import and by the form (fixes "vacation"/"Vacation")
  start_date    DATE NOT NULL,
  end_date      DATE NOT NULL,                   -- inclusive; working days = Mon-Fri in [start,end], holidays NOT excluded, computed never stored
  note          VARCHAR(255) NULL,
  created_at    DATETIME NOT NULL, created_by INT UNSIGNED NULL,
  updated_at    DATETIME NOT NULL, updated_by INT UNSIGNED NULL,
  CONSTRAINT fk_to_emp FOREIGN KEY (employee_id) REFERENCES employees(id),
  CONSTRAINT ck_to_range CHECK (end_date >= start_date),
  KEY ix_to_emp_start (employee_id, start_date),
  KEY ix_to_start (start_date)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;
-- Deleting a request is a hard delete plus a full before-image in audit_log (the sheet lost this history entirely). History screen can re-insert from the snapshot.

CREATE TABLE adjustments (                       -- the "PTO Adjustments" sheet the script supports but nobody ever created
  id            INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
  employee_id   INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  kind          ENUM('PTO','Vacation') NOT NULL,
  effective_date DATE NOT NULL,                  -- selects the cycle: cycle_start <= effective_date < cycle_end (same as sumAdjustments)
  days          DECIMAL(4,1) NOT NULL,           -- + grant, - deduct; half days allowed exactly as the script allowed ("fractional OK")
  reason        VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  created_at    DATETIME NOT NULL, created_by INT UNSIGNED NULL,
  CONSTRAINT fk_adj_emp FOREIGN KEY (employee_id) REFERENCES employees(id),
  KEY ix_adj_emp (employee_id, effective_date)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;

CREATE TABLE calendars (                         -- the five Google Calendars; seeded by setup.php with the IDs from the Apps Script
  cal_key       VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, -- 'pto','birthdays','holidays','factory','sales'
  label         VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL,             -- 'PTO / Vacation','Birthdays','Company Events & Holidays','Factory Closings','End of Month Sale'
  kind          ENUM('pto','birthdays','events') NOT NULL,
  google_calendar_id VARCHAR(160) NULL,
  is_active     TINYINT(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,   -- 'sales' = 0: stale since 2023, still synced so its history stays, hidden from navigation
  dirty         TINYINT(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,   -- set by every write that touches this calendar; cleared by a successful sync
  sort_order    TINYINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;

CREATE TABLE events (                            -- rows of the three [Event Name, Start, End] sheets
  id            INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
  cal_key       VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
  title         VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
  start_date    DATE NOT NULL,
  end_date      DATE NOT NULL,                   -- inclusive; Google receives end+1 (all-day end is exclusive), same as the script
  created_at    DATETIME NOT NULL, created_by INT UNSIGNED NULL,
  updated_at    DATETIME NOT NULL, updated_by INT UNSIGNED NULL,
  CONSTRAINT fk_ev_cal FOREIGN KEY (cal_key) REFERENCES calendars(cal_key),
  CONSTRAINT ck_ev_range CHECK (end_date >= start_date),
  KEY ix_ev_cal_start (cal_key, start_date)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;
-- Birthdays have no table of their own: they are derived from employees (active only) for the current year and next, exactly like addBirthdaysToCalendar.

CREATE TABLE calendar_links (                    -- DB row <-> Google event id. Rebuildable: if lost, the sync adopts matching events by fingerprint instead of duplicating
  id            INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
  cal_key       VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
  source        ENUM('time_off','event','birthday') NOT NULL,
  source_id     INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,           -- time_off.id / events.id / employees.id
  occurrence    SMALLINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, -- birthday year (2026, 2027); 0 otherwise
  google_event_id VARCHAR(120) NOT NULL,
  fingerprint   CHAR(40) NOT NULL,               -- sha1(title|start|end_exclusive); a changed fingerprint means PATCH
  synced_at     DATETIME NOT NULL,
  UNIQUE KEY uq_link (cal_key, source, source_id, occurrence),
  UNIQUE KEY uq_gid  (cal_key, google_event_id)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;

CREATE TABLE sync_runs (                         -- one row per sync attempt; feeds the dashboard status strip
  id            INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
  cal_key       VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
  triggered_by  ENUM('inline','cron','nightly','manual') NOT NULL,
  started_at    DATETIME NOT NULL, finished_at DATETIME NULL,
  n_created INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, n_updated INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, n_deleted INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, n_adopted INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  ok            TINYINT(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  message       VARCHAR(500) NULL,               -- error text, or 'refused: would delete 212 of 240 events' from the safety valve
  KEY ix_runs_cal (cal_key, started_at)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;

CREATE TABLE users (
  id            INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
  username      VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  display_name  VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
  password_hash VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,           -- password_hash(..., PASSWORD_DEFAULT)
  role          ENUM('admin','editor','viewer') NOT NULL DEFAULT 'viewer',
  is_active     TINYINT(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  failed_logins TINYINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  locked_until  DATETIME NULL,
  must_change_password TINYINT(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  last_login_at DATETIME NULL,
  created_at    DATETIME NOT NULL
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;

CREATE TABLE audit_log (                         -- every insert/update/delete on employees, time_off, adjustments, events, users, calendars
  id            BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
  at            DATETIME NOT NULL,
  user_id       INT UNSIGNED NULL,               -- NULL = import or cron
  action        ENUM('insert','update','delete') NOT NULL,
  table_name    VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL,
  row_id        INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  employee_id   INT UNSIGNED NULL,               -- denormalized so "history of this employee" is one indexed query
  before_json   MEDIUMTEXT NULL,                 -- full row snapshot (TEXT, not the JSON type, so MariaDB and MySQL behave identically)
  after_json    MEDIUMTEXT NULL,
  summary       VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,           -- 'Walker, Rebecca: Vacation 2026-10-11..2026-10-13 (3 days) added'
  KEY ix_audit_emp (employee_id, at), KEY ix_audit_at (at)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;

CREATE TABLE settings (                          -- tiny key/value: schema_version, api_key, ics_key, google_token_cache, google_token_expires_at, last_backup_at
  name  VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
  value TEXT NULL
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;

CREATE TABLE api_hits (                          -- answers "does anything still call the old doGet?" After six quiet months, api.php can be deleted
  id INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY, at DATETIME NOT NULL, ip VARCHAR(45) NULL, user_agent VARCHAR(200) NULL
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;

Migrations: numbered files in lib/migrations/; settings.schema_version records the last applied; Admin > "Apply updates" shows pending files and runs them in a transaction. Restoring an older backup then uploading newer code simply re-applies the pending ones.
screens: Login (login.php) — anyone with an account (Chris, the office manager, optionally viewers). Username + password; 5 failed attempts locks the account for 15 minutes; first login with a temporary password forces a change. No email-based reset (an admin sets a new temporary password), so there is no SMTP dependency.

Dashboard (index.php) — the page Chris and the office manager live on; viewers see it read-only. One row per active employee: name, hire date, years of service, current cycle (03/08/2026 – 03/07/2027), PTO left / allotment, Vacation left / allotment (red if negative, amber if 1 or fewer left), and the next-cycle preview in the sheet's own wording: 'After 03/08/2027: 3 PTO / 15 Vac'. Below it: 'Coming up' (all time off and events in the next 30 days) and the calendar-sync status strip ('All 5 calendars in sync, last run 12 min ago' or a red 'PTO calendar sync failed at 09:15: ...' banner). Primary actions: + Time off, + Employee, Sync now.

Time Off list (requests.php) — editors/admins. All requests newest-first with filters for employee, type and cycle/year. Columns mirror the sheet exactly: employee, type, start, end, working days, PTO remaining after, Vacation remaining after, note ('After MM/DD/YYYY: N PTO / N Vac' for next-cycle rows). Row actions: edit, delete (confirm dialog; deletion is audit-logged with a full snapshot). Export CSV.

Time Off form (request.php, new and edit) — editors/admins. Employee picker (active employees only), PTO/Vacation radio, start date, end date (auto-fills to start date), optional note. As soon as dates are picked a live preview line appears: '3 working days -> Vacation 13 of 15 left in cycle 03/08/2026 – 03/07/2027'. Non-blocking warnings, because the sheet never blocked either: 0 working days (weekend only), balance goes negative, overlaps an existing request, spans an anniversary boundary (offers 'split into two rows'), includes a company holiday, starts before hire date, starts after departure date. Save writes the row, logs the audit entry, marks the PTO calendar dirty and syncs it inline; the confirmation says either 'Saved. Calendar updated.' or 'Saved. Calendar will update within 15 minutes.'

Employees (employees.php) — admins/editors. Active employees with hire date, years of service, birthday as MM/DD, current cycle allotments; 'Show former employees' toggle. + Add employee: last name, first name, hire date, birthday month + day (two selects; no year asked for). Saving marks the birthdays calendar dirty.

Employee detail (employee.php?id=N) — admins/editors edit, viewers read. Profile edit; a cycle-by-cycle ledger from hire date through the next cycle: allotment, adjustments, used, remaining, and every request with its running balance (the sheet's E/F/G columns, grouped by cycle); an Adjustments panel (+ grant / deduct N days, type, effective date, reason required); 'Mark as departed on <date>' which keeps all history and past calendar events, removes the person from pickers, dashboard, api.php and future birthday events.
Adjustments (adjustments.php) — admins. Cross-employee list of every grant/deduction with reason, effective date and the cycle it landed in; add from here or from the employee page.

Events (events.php?cal=holidays | factory | sales) — editors/admins. One tab per event calendar (the three [name, start, end] sheets): a table with an inline add row at the top, edit and delete per row. 'sales' is archived (is_active=0), hidden from the nav until re-activated in Admin; its 5 rows are still migrated so the old calendar's history is not deleted by the sync.

History (history.php) — admins/editors. The audit log: when, who, what (before -> after), filterable by employee, table, user and date. 'Restore' on deleted time-off rows re-inserts from the stored snapshot (milestone 3).

Admin (admin.php) — admins only. Users (add, role, reset temporary password, deactivate). Calendars (the five Google calendar IDs, active flag, 'Test connection', 'Sync now' per calendar or all, the sync run log, and a 'Force' button to override the mass-delete safety valve after you have read its message). Self-test (runs tests/balance_test.php in the browser: 'Balance engine: 177/177 sheet rows match, 15/15 current balances match' in green, or red with the first mismatch). Backup now / download latest .sql.gz and .json. Apply schema updates. API key and ICS key show/rotate. Footer shows app version and PHP version.

JSON API (api.php?key=<long random>) — machines only, no session. Returns the same array and keys as the old doGet ('employee', 'anniversaryDate', 'remainingPTO', 'remainingVacation', 'remainingPTOCurrent', 'remainingVacationCurrent', 'remainingPTONext', 'remainingVacationNext', 'afterDate'), active employees only. Every hit is logged to api_hits so the unknown consumer, if any, identifies itself; the old Apps Script doGet is rewritten to fetch and pass this through so its URL keeps working. Also serves api.php?action=preview for the form's live balance line (session-authenticated).

ICS feeds (ics.php?cal=pto&k=<key>, milestone 3, optional) — five read-only iCal feeds generated straight from the database. Nobody needs them while the Google Calendars are synced; they are the escape hatch if the Google side is ever retired, since every phone calendar app can subscribe to an ICS URL.
balance_engine:
WHERE: lib/balance.php, a single file of pure functions with zero database access. It takes plain arrays (one employee, that employee's time_off rows, that employee's adjustments) plus an explicit $today DateTimeImmutable and returns arrays. Every screen, api.php and the self-test call the same functions; nothing else in the codebase does date arithmetic on cycles. Because $today is a parameter, the test suite is deterministic and the sheet snapshot from 2026-09-14 stays valid forever.

HOW (a line-for-line port of the six Apps Script functions, same names so the two can be diffed side by side):
- years_of_service_at($asOf, $hire): $asOf->year - $hire->year, minus 1 if $asOf's (month, day) is before $hire's (month, day). Not clamped at zero, exactly like the script (negative years yield allotment 0 anyway).
- vacation_allotment_for($yos): >=10 -> 15, >=5 -> 10, >=1 -> 5, else 0. pto_allotment_for($yos): >=1 -> 3 else 0. Both read from a const table at the top of the file.
- cycle_for($ref, $hire): anniversaryThisYear = setDate($ref->year, $hire->month, $hire->day); start = anniversaryThisYear <= $ref ? anniversaryThisYear : same date in $ref->year - 1; end = start + 1 year (exclusive). A request starting ON the anniversary belongs to the new cycle, as in the script.
- working_days($start, $end): iterate inclusive dates, count where format('N') <= 5. Holidays are not excluded; no half days.
- sum_adjustments($adjustments, $cycleStart, $cycleEnd, $kind): sum days where cycleStart <= effective_date < cycleEnd.
- compute_employee($employee, $requests, $adjustments, $today): sorts requests by start_date then id (the script's stable tiebreak), walks them, resets running totals whenever the cycle key changes, allotment = tier(years_of_service_at(cycleStart)) + adjustments in that cycle, subtracts working_days per request, and records per request: cycle_start, cycle_end, days, pto_remaining, vac_remaining, note ('After MM/DD/YYYY: N PTO / N Vac' when cycle_start equals the cycle after today's). It also returns cycle summaries (allot, used, adjustments, remaining) for every cycle from hire date through today's-cycle + 1, and the current/next cycle numbers that the dashboard and api.php show (the script's computeCycleRemaining with offsets 0 and 1).
- Numbers are handled as floats formatted with a helper that prints '3' not '3.0' and '2.5' when an adjustment introduced a half day; the sheet already allowed this.

HOW IT STAYS IDENTICAL TO THE SHEET:
1. tests/fixtures/sheet_snapshot_2026-09-14.json holds the 15 employees, all 177 rows including the sheet's stored E/F values, and the 15 expected current-cycle balances from the brief (Walker R 2/3 14/15, Catuto 3/3 12/15, ... Walker J 2/3 0/5, six 2026 hires 0/0).
2. tests/balance_test.php feeds them through compute_employee with $today = 2026-09-14 and asserts 177/177 per-row matches and 15/15 balances, plus hand-written edge cases: the Saturday-only row (Danalewich 2026-05-16 = 0 days), the 6-working-day request, a request starting exactly on an anniversary (new cycle), a request the day before (old cycle), a Dec 31 / Jan 1 boundary, a request before hire date (allotment 0, negative balance, no crash), a half-day adjustment, and a Feb-29 hire (PHP setDate rolls Feb 29 to Mar 1 in non-leap years exactly as JS Date does, so parity holds; no such employee exists today).
3. The test runs from the command line on XAMPP (php tests/balance_test.php) before every upload, and from Admin > Self-test on the server after every PHP version bump. Both print the same one-line verdict.
4. The Python re-implementation that produced the 0-mismatch result today is kept in tools/ as a second independent oracle for the next time the rules are questioned.
5. Rule changes (a new tier, a policy start date) are made in balance.php only, with a new fixture; if tiers ever change for future cycles only, the const becomes an array keyed by effective date and cycle_for picks the row in effect at cycle start. That is the one foreseeable extension and it is a 20-line change.
calendar_sync:
DECISION: keep all five Google Calendars, strictly as a read-only mirror of the database, and add ICS feeds later as the fallback. Reasoning from the operations lens: everyone already has the five calendars on their phones with notifications configured; the delete-and-recreate semantics they rely on today are cheap to reproduce; the cost of keeping them is one service account created once and about 180 lines of PHP. The alternative (an in-app calendar page plus ICS subscriptions) would require re-subscribing 15 phones, and Google Calendar refreshes external ICS feeds only every 12-24 hours, which is a visible regression from today's near-immediate updates. So: Google Calendars stay the display layer; the database is the only source of truth; nobody edits the calendars directly (anything added there by hand is deleted on the next sync, exactly as today, and the Admin page says so in bold).

AUTH: a Google Cloud service account (lsp-pto-sync@...iam.gserviceaccount.com) whose JSON key sits in pto_data/. Each of the five calendars is shared with that address with "Make changes to events". lib/calendar.php builds an RS256 JWT (header, claims iss/scope=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.events/aud/iat/exp, signed with openssl_sign using the key's private_key), POSTs it to https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token, and caches the access token in settings for 55 minutes. No consent screen, no refresh tokens, no domain-wide delegation, nothing that expires. If the Workspace admin policy forbids service-account keys, the fallback is a one-time OAuth consent page (google_auth.php) that stores a refresh token; Workspace-internal apps' refresh tokens do not expire. Only the token function changes.

MAPPING (all-day events, date fields only, no time zone juggling, which removes the script's toLocaleString hack):
- pto calendar: one event per time_off row, title '<Last>, <First> - <PTO|Vacation>', start = start_date, end = end_date + 1. Departed employees' past rows are still mirrored (history stays).
- birthdays calendar: for each active employee, current year and next year, title '<Last>, <First> Birthday', description 'Birthday'. Earlier years are deleted each sync, as today.
- holidays / factory / sales calendars: one event per events row, title as typed, end + 1.
Each created event carries extendedProperties.private.lsp = 'time_off:123' so it is recognizable even if calendar_links is lost.

ALGORITHM (lib/sync.php, sync_calendar($cal_key, $trigger)), guarded by MySQL GET_LOCK('pto_sync_<cal_key>', 0) so cron and an inline run never overlap:
1. Build desired[] from the DB: key -> {title, start, end_exclusive, fingerprint}.
2. Load links[] for the calendar and remote[] from Google (one GET events list, maxResults=2500, timeMin 2021-01-01, timeMax 2040-01-01, singleEvents=true, fields limited to id/summary/start/end/extendedProperties; paginate if nextPageToken ever appears).
3. For each desired item: if a link exists and remote still has that id and fingerprints match -> nothing; if link exists but fingerprint differs -> PATCH title/start/end and update the link; if no link -> look for an unclaimed remote event with the same fingerprint and ADOPT it (write a link, no API call); otherwise INSERT and write the link.
4. Every remote event not claimed by a link is DELETED; link rows whose key is no longer desired are removed. This preserves the sheet-is-source-of-truth behavior.
5. Safety valve: if step 4 would delete more than 20 events AND more than 50% of the calendar, abort before deleting anything, record ok=0 with 'refused: would delete N of M events; check the calendar ID and make sure the old Apps Script triggers are off', mark the calendar dirty and show the red banner. Admin > Force runs it anyway after a human reads that message.
6. Record a sync_runs row with counts; on success clear calendars.dirty.

TRIGGERS: every write sets dirty=1 on the affected calendar and, on the same request, calls sync_calendar($key, 'inline') inside try/catch with a 10-second curl budget, so a saved request is on everyone's phone within seconds like today. cron/sync.php every 15 minutes syncs whatever is still dirty (the safety net when the inline run failed or timed out). cron/sync.php --all at 03:05 reconciles all five regardless (catches manual edits people made in Google, exactly like the script's full pass). Admin > Sync now triggers a manual run.

FAILURE HANDLING: HTTP 401 -> refresh token once and retry; 403 rateLimitExceeded / 5xx -> sleep 1s, 2s, 4s then give up for this run; 404 on PATCH/DELETE -> drop the link and let the next pass re-insert; network down -> ok=0, calendar stays dirty, cron retries; adopt-by-fingerprint makes a restored-from-backup calendar_links table harmless (no duplicates). The dashboard strip turns red when the latest run for any active calendar failed or when a calendar has been dirty for more than 30 minutes, so the person entering data sees the problem without reading logs. Sync detail is also appended to pto_data/logs/sync.log (one line per run, rotated at 5 MB).

CUTOVER DETAIL: the first sync against the real calendars adopts every event whose title/dates already match, so the 177 PTO events, the ~40 event rows and the birthdays are not churned. The only forced churn is the rows whose type was stored as lowercase 'vacation': their titles change to '... - Vacation', so those events are deleted and recreated once. The old Apps Script's time-based triggers MUST be deleted before this first sync (two writers with delete-everything-else semantics would fight); the safety valve is there in case that step is forgotten.

ICS (milestone 3): ics.php?cal=<key>&k=<ics_key> emits VCALENDAR with the same all-day events from the DB, Cache-Control 15 minutes. Documented in README as 'if we ever leave Google Calendar, subscribe to these five URLs'.
auth:
WHO: three roles in the users table. admin (Chris): everything, including users, calendars, imports, backups, schema updates. editor (the office manager, e.g. Krisanne): employees, time off, adjustments, events, history. viewer (optional, any staff member who wants to see the balance table without asking): dashboard and employee ledgers read-only. Start with two accounts; the calendars remain the read channel for everyone else, so most staff never log in.

PASSWORDS: password_hash()/password_verify() with PASSWORD_DEFAULT (bcrypt today, upgrades itself via password_needs_rehash on login when PHP changes the default). Minimum 12 characters. No self-service reset and therefore no outbound email dependency: an admin sets a temporary password from Admin > Users and the user is forced to change it at next login (must_change_password). Lockout: 5 failed logins -> locked_until = now + 15 minutes, per account; the login page says only 'invalid username or password' and 'try again in N minutes'. All failed and successful logins are audit-logged.

SESSIONS: PHP's native file sessions (cPanel already provides the per-account session directory). bootstrap sets session.cookie_secure=1, cookie_httponly=1, cookie_samesite=Lax, use_strict_mode=1, gc_maxlifetime=43200 (12 hours idle); session_regenerate_id(true) on login and on privilege change; logout destroys the session. A CSRF token is created per session and required as a hidden field on every POST (checked in bootstrap before any handler runs). Every screen starts with require_login() and, where relevant, require_role('editor') or require_role('admin'); api.php uses the static key from settings instead of a session and is rate-limited to 60 requests/minute per IP by a tiny counter in settings.

HARDENING THAT COSTS NOTHING: HTTPS forced by cPanel; security headers (X-Frame-Options DENY, X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, Referrer-Policy same-origin, a strict CSP allowing only self, which works because there are no CDNs) sent from bootstrap; display_errors off with errors logged to pto_data/logs/error.log and a friendly error page carrying a reference id; PDO with prepared statements everywhere and ERRMODE_EXCEPTION; output escaped through a single h() helper. Optional extra layer if wanted later: cPanel > Directory Privacy on pto_web adds HTTP Basic auth in front of the whole app with zero code.
migration:
SOURCE: a fresh export of the workbook on cutover day (File > Download > CSV for each of the five sheets, or the existing xlsx_dump.json, which tools/import_sheet.php also accepts). The import is a page under Admin (also runnable as a CLI script on XAMPP) with a dry-run report and a commit button, so it is rehearsed locally first and then run once on the server.

STEP 1, dry run (no writes): parse each sheet; normalize. Employee names 'Last, First' split on the first comma into last_name/first_name (trimmed). Hire dates copied. Birthdays keep only month and day (the 2023 placeholder years for the nine older staff and the real years for the six 2026 hires are both discarded on purpose). Time off: type lower-cased then mapped to 'PTO'/'Vacation' (fixes the 'vacation' rows); rows referencing a name not on the employee sheet are listed as errors and block commit; start > end blocks commit; the Saturday-only row (Danalewich 2026-05-16) and the 6-working-day row are imported unchanged and merely listed as warnings, because the sheet counts them that way and the calendar shows them today. Event sheets: all rows imported verbatim into events with cal_key holidays/factory/sales, including the misc 2023 items sitting on the Factory Closings sheet (Thanksgiving luncheon, Christmas party, sale notes); they stay on the factory calendar exactly as they are now and can be moved from the Events screen later. The report prints counts (15 employees, 177 requests, 12 holiday rows, 26 factory rows, 5 sales rows) and every warning.

STEP 2, commit: one transaction inserting employees, time_off, events (adjustments table stays empty: the sheet never had one) with created_by NULL and audit_log rows summarized 'imported from LSP Calendar Update 2026-xx-xx'. The import refuses to run if time_off already has rows unless 'replace all' is ticked, so it cannot be double-run by accident.

STEP 3, verify against the sheet (this is the acceptance test): Admin > Self-test runs balance_test.php against the fixture built from the same export (the stored E/F values of all 177 rows and the sheet's D/E allotment columns) and must print 177/177 rows and 15/15 employees matching. tools/verify_import.php additionally prints a side-by-side table: employee, sheet PTO remaining, app PTO remaining, sheet Vacation remaining, app Vacation remaining, with a DIFF column, so Chris can eyeball it. The numbers expected today are the ones in the brief (Walker R 2/3 and 14/15 ... Walker J 2/3 and 0/5, six 2026 hires 0/0). Also compare the dashboard row-by-row with the calendar for two employees by hand.

STEP 4, calendar rehearsal (one week, optional but recommended): point the five calendar IDs at five throwaway calendars created for the test, run Sync now, open them on a phone, and confirm events and titles look identical to the real ones. During this week the sheet stays live and the office manager enters new requests in both places (roughly 4 rows a week, so cheap).

STEP 5, cutover (a Friday evening): in the Apps Script editor delete every time-based trigger and rename the sheet 'LSP Calendar Update (ARCHIVED 2026-xx-xx, replaced by pto.lightsaberpromotions.com)', keep it read-only as a historical reference. Re-export and re-import with 'replace all' so the week's new rows are included, re-run the self-test. Paste the five real calendar IDs into Admin > Calendars, Test connection, Sync now (all). Expected result: adopted counts roughly equal to the row counts, created/deleted only for the lowercase 'vacation' rows and stale prior-year birthdays; anything larger trips the safety valve and is investigated before Force. Replace the Apps Script doGet body with a one-line UrlFetchApp.fetch of api.php?key=... so the old JSON URL keeps working and api_hits starts recording whether anyone uses it.

STEP 6, first Monday: the office manager enters the week's requests in the app only; Chris checks the dashboard against what she would have expected from the sheet. After a month of clean audit history, the sheet is left archived.
deployment:
INITIAL DEPLOY: steps 1-8 in hosting_fit, in that order; the whole thing is done through the cPanel web UI and a browser. README.md in pto_web is that same list verbatim, with the placeholders filled in, so the runbook lives next to the code and in every backup.

LOCAL MIRROR: XAMPP with C:\xampp\htdocs\pto_web and C:\xampp\htdocs\pto_data (sibling rule, identical to the server), a local MySQL database created with the same lib/migrations, a local config.php pointing calendars at the throwaway test calendars or with google_enabled=false so no sync runs from the laptop. The same setup.php creates the local admin.

UPDATE PROCEDURE (every change, ten minutes, no SSH):
1. Edit locally, browse it on XAMPP, run php tests\balance_test.php and confirm the green line.
2. If the change needs a schema change, add lib/migrations/00N_description.sql (forward-only, idempotent where possible). Bump APP_VERSION in lib/bootstrap.php.
3. Zip the pto_web folder (pto_web-2026-10-01.zip). Keep the previous zip; that is the rollback.
4. cPanel > File Manager > upload the zip to /home/<cpuser>/ > Extract (overwrites files in place; pto_data is untouched because it is a sibling folder). Delete the zip.
5. Log in, open Admin: if migrations are pending a yellow bar says so; click Apply updates. Click Self-test. Done. Rollback = extract the previous zip (and, only if a migration must be undone, restore last night's database backup through phpMyAdmin > Import).
A deploy touching only PHP/CSS/JS is atomic enough for a 15-user tool; the 15-minute cron is the only concurrent process and it takes a DB lock before it syncs.

BACKUPS (three independent layers):
1. cron/backup.php nightly at 03:20: a pure-PHP dump (SELECT every table, write INSERT statements; no dependency on exec() or mysqldump being on PATH) to pto_data/backups/pto-YYYY-MM-DD.sql.gz plus pto-YYYY-MM-DD.json (employees, time off, adjustments, events as plain JSON, the ten-year exit format anyone can read). Retention: last 60 daily, plus the first of every month forever (a few KB each). Writes last_backup_at to settings; the dashboard strip goes red if it is older than 48 hours.
2. Admin > Backup now / Download latest, for the moment before a risky edit.
3. Liquid Web / cPanel account backups (Backup or JetBackup in cPanel, whichever the account has) already cover both the MySQL database and /home/<cpuser>/pto_data; verify once that pto_data is inside the backed-up paths.
Restore drill (do it once, on XAMPP): create an empty DB, phpMyAdmin > Import the .sql.gz, point config.php at it, log in. Twenty minutes; write the result into README.

CRON: the three entries listed in hosting_fit (*/15 sync of dirty calendars; 03:05 full reconcile; 03:20 backup), all using /opt/cpanel/ea-php84/root/usr/bin/php. When the MultiPHP version is bumped, the cron paths are the one other place that must be edited; cron/sync.php prints PHP_VERSION into cron.log so a mismatch is visible, and Admin shows the PHP version the web side runs.

MONITORING WITHOUT A MONITORING SYSTEM: the dashboard strip (sync status, last backup age) is seen every time someone enters a request; error.log and sync.log in pto_data/logs; cron.log rotated by size. Optional: cPanel cron's own 'email output to' setting pointed at chris@ for any cron run that prints 'ERROR'.

TEN-YEAR MAINTENANCE CALENDAR: yearly, open MultiPHP Manager and move to the newest 8.x, then click Self-test and fix the cron path; yearly, confirm AutoSSL is still renewing; every two years, rotate the service-account key (create new key, upload, delete old) and the api/ics keys; whenever an employee leaves, use Mark as departed instead of delete.
risks: Two writers on the same calendars: if the old Apps Script's time-based triggers are left on after cutover, the sheet and the app will each delete the other's events every run. Mitigation: trigger deletion is the first line of the cutover checklist, the sheet is renamed ARCHIVED, and the sync's mass-delete safety valve refuses to remove more than 20 events and 50% of a calendar without a human clicking Force.

Google Workspace policy may forbid creating service-account keys (iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation). Mitigation: the token function is isolated in lib/calendar.php; fallback is a one-time OAuth consent page storing a non-expiring Workspace-internal refresh token; last resort is ICS feeds with no Google API at all.

PHP version drift over ten years (cPanel/EasyApache retires old 8.x versions and Liquid Web may migrate the server). Mitigation: no framework and no vendor code to age; code kept 8.2-8.5 clean; Admin > Self-test after every bump; cron paths are the one manual edit and are logged.

Bus factor of one: Chris is the only person who understands the code. Mitigation: roughly 2,500 lines of plain PHP with README.md as a literal runbook, the JSON nightly export as a vendor-neutral exit format, and the Python oracle for the rules; any PHP freelancer can take it over.

Balance policy change (tiers, PTO count, holidays excluded, half days) would silently rewrite historical balances if applied naively. Mitigation: tiers are a const with a documented extension to effective-dated rows; the fixture test would fail loudly on any unintended change; the holiday-overlap warning in the form deliberately does not alter the count, preserving parity with the sheet until the business decides otherwise.

Cycle-straddling requests: the rule (all days counted in the cycle containing the start date) is preserved, but it can look wrong to a human. Mitigation: the form warns and offers to split into two rows; no data does this today.

api.php consumer unknown: the JSON shape is preserved but anniversaryDate is emitted as YYYY-MM-DD rather than the Apps Script's ISO timestamp, which could break a consumer that parses the old format. Mitigation: the doGet URL is kept as a passthrough, api_hits records any caller, and the field can be re-formatted in five minutes if a consumer surfaces.

Loss of calendar_links (e.g. restoring an older backup) could in principle duplicate events. Mitigation: adopt-by-fingerprint and the extendedProperties marker make the sync self-healing; the nightly full reconcile catches anything missed.
Google Calendar API quota or deprecation: v3 has been stable since 2011 and five calendars with ~300 events are far below any quota; the ICS fallback exists for the day Google changes its mind.

Manual edits in Google Calendar by staff are deleted on the next sync (same as today). Mitigation: stated in bold on the Admin page and in README; the events screen is the place to add company events.

Inline sync adds 1-3 seconds to saving a request when Google is slow, and if the 10-second budget is exceeded the calendar lags up to 15 minutes. Mitigation: the confirmation message says which happened; cron catches up; nothing is lost because the DB is the source of truth.
Birthday year is discarded on migration, so age is not available if anyone ever wants it. Acceptable: the current data's years are placeholders and only month/day is used anywhere.
cPanel cron using the wrong PHP binary (/usr/local/bin/php) can run an older PHP silently. Mitigation: explicit ea-php path in the cron lines and PHP_VERSION printed to cron.log on every run.

Session cookies on a subdomain of the company site are isolated by host, but if the main site ever moves to the same host path, cookie names could collide. Mitigation: session_name('lsp_pto') set in bootstrap.
effort:
Build effort for one person who already knows PHP, working evenings and a couple of weekend mornings: about 50-60 hours across 3-4 weeks.

MILESTONE 1, the first usable thing (about 25 hours, week 1-2): schema 001, bootstrap/auth/CSRF/layout, employees list + form, time off list + form with live preview, dashboard with balances and next-cycle notes, audit log, tests/balance_test.php green against the 177-row fixture, and the import tool with dry-run. At this point the app runs on XAMPP and on the server in shadow mode: the sheet is still live and syncing calendars, the app shows the same numbers, and the office manager can already use the dashboard as the answer to 'how many days do I have left'. This is the point at which you know the design is right, because the fixture test either says 177/177 or it does not.

MILESTONE 2, cutover-ready (about 15 hours, week 2-3): lib/calendar.php (JWT + REST), lib/sync.php (diff, adopt, safety valve), events screens for the three calendars, birthdays, dirty flags, inline and cron triggers, sync status strip, cutover checklist executed on test calendars and then the real ones. After this the sheet is archived.

MILESTONE 3, finish and forget (about 12 hours, week 3-4): adjustments, mark-as-departed, history with restore, nightly backup + download, self-test in Admin, api.php with hit logging and the doGet passthrough, ICS feeds, migrations runner, README runbook, restore drill.

Ongoing cost: minutes per week for the office manager entering requests; for Chris, one yearly PHP-version bump plus whatever a rule change needs. No hosting cost beyond the existing Liquid Web account; the Google Cloud project is free at this usage.

title: LSP Time Off: plain-PHP + MySQL time-off board on cPanel, designed from the office screens backwards
lens: USER-FIRST. Three people drive every decision: the admin who must record 'Nikki, PTO, Friday' in under 10 seconds; the employee who opens a phone and wants one number (days left, and when the year resets); and the whole office, who glance at who is out, birthdays, holidays and factory closings on their phones without adopting anything new (they keep the five Google Calendars). The stack was chosen last, by asking what serves those screens with the least setup on a stock cPanel and the least code for one PHP developer to maintain alone.
stack: PHP 8.2 (cPanel ea-php82; 8.3 if MultiPHP offers it). Extensions needed are all in the default EasyApache profile: pdo_mysql, mbstring, openssl, curl, json. No framework, no Composer, no vendor/: about 3,000 lines of plain PHP (public/index.php front controller, 40-line regex router, PDO prepared statements, PHP templates with esc(), 10-line spl_autoload_register over src/). Why: Chris already maintains small PHP tools; Composer on cPanel needs SSH or a committed vendor tree; plain PHP 8 code will run unchanged for years. Database: MySQL/MariaDB from the cPanel 'MySQL Databases' page (the real database he asked for), InnoDB, utf8mb4, DATE columns for every calendar date (never DATETIME for dates); phpMyAdmin already exists for inspection; SQLite would be a one-line DSN change. Front-end: server-rendered HTML, one mobile-first CSS file (~400 lines, 4-icon bottom nav on phones), one vanilla JS file (~250 lines) used only for progressive enhancement (live working-day count and balance preview on the add form, calendar filter toggles, Enter-to-save). Native input type=date gives phone date pickers free. PWA manifest so staff can Add to Home Screen. No build step, no npm, no CDN dependency. Google Calendar API v3 called with curl + openssl_sign (RS256 service-account JWT), ~120 lines, no SDK. Local dev on XAMPP (PHP 8.2 + MariaDB) runs the identical code.
hosting_fit: 1) cPanel > Subdomains: create timeoff.lightsaberpromotions.com with document root /home/CPUSER/timeoff/public (app code lives above the web root). AutoSSL issues the certificate automatically. 2) cPanel > MultiPHP Manager: set that subdomain to ea-php82 (or 83). Confirm via /admin/health page which prints PHP version and required extensions. 3) cPanel > MySQL Databases: create database CPUSER_timeoff, user CPUSER_timeoff with a generated password, grant ALL PRIVILEGES. 4) Get the code onto the server: preferred cPanel > Git Version Control > Create, clone the private GitHub repo over HTTPS (personal access token), repository path /home/CPUSER/timeoff; the repo's .cpanel.yml deploys on 'Pull or Deploy'. Fallback: File Manager, upload release zip, Extract into /home/CPUSER/timeoff. 5) File Manager: copy config/config.sample.php to config/config.php, fill DB name/user/password, app_key (random 32 chars), timezone America/New_York, admin email. 6) Browse to https://timeoff.../install once: runs migrations/*.sql, creates the first admin (Chris), then disables itself (writes storage/installed.lock). 7) Google (one time, ~20 min): Google Cloud Console > new project 'LSP Time Off' > enable Google Calendar API > create Service Account > create JSON key; upload key to /home/CPUSER/timeoff/config/google-sa.json (chmod 600, above web root). In Google Calendar, for each of the five calendars > Settings > Share with specific people > add the service-account email with 'Make changes to events'. Paste the five calendar IDs (already known from the script) into /admin/settings. 8) cPanel > Cron Jobs: add the three lines listed under deployment, using /opt/cpanel/ea-php82/root/usr/bin/php so cron and web use the same PHP. 9) Nothing else: no php.ini edits, no SSH, no Node, no Docker, no extra Apache modules (mod_rewrite is on; public/.htaccess routes everything to index.php).
screens: Login (everyone): email + password, Remember me for 60 days so phones rarely see it again; Forgot password sends a one-time link. Nothing else on the page.

Home / Who's Out (everyone, the app's landing page and the phone view): three cards - Today, This week, Next week - listing 'Rebecca Walker - Vacation (Thu-Fri)', then Upcoming birthdays, Company holidays, Factory closings for the next 30 days. Staff see a My Balance card ('2 of 3 PTO, 14 of 15 Vacation left; resets Mar 8, 2027'). Admins get a sticky '+ Time off' button. Primary actions: tap a person to open their page; tap + to add.

Add Time Off (admin, the 10-second screen): employee select autofocused (active employees only, alphabetical, last-used first); PTO | Vacation as two big segmented buttons; Start date; End date auto-fills to Start (most rows are one day). As you type, the live preview reads 'Thu Oct 2 - Fri Oct 3 : 2 working days : Nikki will have 13 of 15 Vacation left (year Aug 10, 2026 - Aug 9, 2027)'. Inline warnings: 'No working days in this range' (the Saturday-only case), 'Overlaps her PTO on Oct 2', 'Would go to -1 PTO' (allowed, matching the sheet), 'Falls in next year: After 08/10/2027: 3 PTO / 15 Vac'. Enter saves; toast 'Saved. Calendar updated.' with 10-second Undo; form resets keeping the employee so several days can be entered quickly.

Balances (admins; staff only if the setting allows): one row or card per active employee: name, years of service, current year dates, 'PTO 2 of 3 left', 'Vacation 14 of 15 left' with progress bars, combined total, next anniversary in N days. Toggle This year / Next year (next-year numbers include already-booked next-cycle requests). Sort by name or by days left; Print and Export CSV. Tap a row for the employee page.

Employee page / ledger (admins; staff for their own): header 'Rebecca Walker : hired Mar 8, 2012 (14 yrs) : year resets Mar 8, 2027 : birthday Feb 18'. Sections per anniversary year, newest first, each listing requests in date order with the running balance after each one - exactly the sheet's E/F columns - and adjustments shown inline with their reason; next-year requests carry the 'After 03/08/2027: N PTO / N Vac' note (column G). Actions: Add time off (prefilled), Add adjustment, Edit / Delete a request, Edit employee, Mark departed.

Office Calendar (everyone): month grid with colored chips - PTO blue, Vacation green, Birthday pink, Company event gray, Factory closing orange - filter checkboxes per calendar, prev/next month, Today. On phones it becomes an agenda list grouped by day. Admins tap a chip to edit the underlying row. This is the same data the five Google Calendars show, so it doubles as the sync sanity check.

Employees list + Add/Edit Employee (admin): list with hire date, years, birthday, status, login status. Form: first name, last name, hire date, birthday as Month + Day dropdowns with optional Year (placeholders are gone), 'Create login and email invite' checkbox. Mark departed asks for a date; former employees stay listed under 'Former' with history intact.

Events (admin): three tabs - Company holidays & parties, Factory closings, End-of-month sales - each a simple dated list with an inline add row (title, start, end) and 'Copy last year's events to 2027' for the fixed holidays.

Adjustments (admin): grant or deduct N days (fractional allowed) of PTO or Vacation with an effective date (which picks the anniversary year) and a required reason; shows the resulting balance before saving.

My Time Off (staff): my current-year balances big and plain, my requests in date order with running balance, my next-year note, and my upcoming days. Read-only; the message at the bottom says who to ask to book time.

Admin > Settings & Sync: the five calendar IDs and colors, sync on/off per calendar, sync status (pending, errors, last success time), 'Sync now', 'Dry run' (shows the create/update/delete plan without touching Google), JSON API key, staff-visibility setting, 'Run self-test' (re-checks the engine against the archived sheet fixture), 'Download backup'.

Admin > Users & History: users list with role admin/staff, link to employee, Send invite / Reset password / Deactivate; History shows the audit log ('Chris changed Ketter, Melanie Vacation 10/03-10/09 to 10/03-10/06 on Sep 14 10:22').
balance_engine: One file, src/Balance.php, a straight port of the script, function for function, with the same names so the two can be read side by side: yearsOfServiceAt(asOf, hire), anniversaryWindowFor(ref, hire) returning [start, end) with end = start + 1 year, vacationAllotmentFor(yos) 0/5/10/15 at <1/1-4/5-9/10+, ptoAllotmentFor(yos) 0 or 3, workingDays(start, end) counting Mon-Fri inclusive with holidays NOT excluded, sumAdjustments(adjs, cycleStart, cycleEnd, type), cycleRemaining(employee, today, offset) for the current/next figures (request belongs to the cycle containing its START date), and ledger(employee) which reproduces calculateRemainingDays: sort requests by start_date then id, reset allotment and running totals when the cycle changes, subtract working days, and attach the 'After MM/DD/YYYY: N PTO / N Vac' note when the cycle start equals today's cycle start + 1 year. Dates are DateTimeImmutable built from Y-m-d strings with date_default_timezone_set('America/New_York'); Feb-29 anniversaries roll to Mar 1 exactly like the JS Date constructor. Nothing is stored: balances are recomputed from employees + time_off + adjustments on every page (15 employees x ~200 rows is under a millisecond), so there is no stale-cache state, same as the sheet. Where it runs: server-side only; the add form's live preview calls GET /api/preview (session-authenticated) which runs the same class, so the number the admin sees before saving is the number the ledger shows after. How it stays identical: the migration ships tests/fixtures/sheet_2026-09-14.json (the 177 rows plus the sheet's stored E/F/G values and the 15 current/next balances) and tests/verify.php asserts 0 mismatches; it runs from the CLI and from /admin/selftest, and it stays in the repo forever as the regression test whenever Balance.php is touched.
calendar_sync: Decision: keep all five Google Calendars, unchanged IDs, still shared read-only to staff. Reason: every phone in the office already shows them with notifications; replacing them with ICS subscription feeds would make Google refresh only every 12-24 hours ('I just booked Friday' would not appear until tomorrow), and an app-only calendar would force 15 people to adopt a new habit. The app's own /calendar page is the master view; Google stays a broadcast mirror and nobody edits in Google. Auth mechanism: a Google Cloud service account (JSON key in config/google-sa.json, above the web root). src/Google/ServiceAccount.php builds an RS256 JWT (iss = client_email, scope = https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar, aud = token_uri, 60-minute exp) signed with openssl_sign, exchanges it for an access token with curl, caches the token in storage/cache for 55 minutes. Each calendar is shared with the service-account address with 'Make changes to events', so no OAuth consent screens, no refresh tokens that expire, no user login to keep alive. Model: the database is the source of truth, exactly like the sheet. A desired-set builder derives what each calendar should contain: time_off rows -> all-day event titled 'Last, First - PTO|Vacation' from start_date to end_date+1 (exclusive end, as the script does); active employees' birthdays -> 'Last, First Birthday' for this year and next; events rows -> title, start, end+1. Each desired item is upserted into calendar_mirror with a fingerprint (sha1 of title|start|end); changed fingerprints become pending, desired items missing from the mirror become pending inserts, mirror rows with no desired item become delete_pending. Every app-created event carries extendedProperties.private.lsp = 'time_off:123' so reconciliation never depends on title matching again. Triggering: after a save commits, the app tries an inline push for that one calendar with an 8-second curl budget (so the toast can truthfully say 'Calendar updated'); if Google is slow or down the row simply stays pending and the cron picks it up within 15 minutes. Cron */15 runs bin/sync.php (pending only); nightly bin/sync.php --full lists every event 2021-2040 on each calendar and reconciles, generating next year's birthdays and deleting events not present in the database - the same 'sheet is truth' semantics as today - but guarded: a run that would delete more than 25 events or 20% of a calendar aborts and emails Chris unless --force, and 'Dry run' in Settings shows the plan first. First run is an adopt run: existing Google events are matched by title+dates to database rows and their google_event_ids recorded, so staff do not see 250 events deleted and recreated (only the 4 lowercase 'vacation' titles and one trailing-space factory title get rewritten). Failure handling: state=error with last_error and attempts, retry backoff 15 min x attempts capped at 6 hours, banner on the admin home ('Calendar sync: 2 pending, last success 10:32'), email after 3 consecutive failures, 'Sync now' button. The legacy doGet JSON contract is preserved at GET /api/balances.json?key=... with identical keys (employee, anniversaryDate, remainingPTO, remainingVacation, remainingPTOCurrent, remainingVacationCurrent, remainingPTONext, remainingVacationNext, afterDate); during transition the Apps Script doGet body is replaced by a UrlFetchApp proxy to that URL so whatever consumes the old URL keeps working. Optional bonus, not required for cutover: GET /ical/{token}/timeoff.ics feeds for anyone on Apple or Outlook calendars.
auth: Who: every employee can have a login; two roles. admin (Chris plus the office manager, at least two so nobody is locked out) can do everything; staff is read-only: Who's Out, Office Calendar, My Time Off, and the office-wide Balances only if the admin setting staff_can_see_all_balances is on (default off: who is out is already public via the calendars, remaining balances are not). Accounts are created from the Employee form ('Create login and email invite'); the invite is a one-time set-password link (SHA-256 token hash, 24-hour expiry) sent with PHP mail() through cPanel's Exim; fallback if mail is flaky: admin sets a temporary password shown once on screen. Passwords: password_hash with PASSWORD_DEFAULT (bcrypt), minimum 10 characters, verified with password_verify. Sessions: native PHP sessions with cookie flags Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, session_regenerate_id on login, 8-hour idle timeout; Remember me uses a selector/validator cookie pair (validator hashed in remember_tokens, 60 days) so phones stay signed in. CSRF: per-session token in every POST form checked by the router. Brute force: login_attempts table, 5 failures per email or IP in 15 minutes locks for 15 minutes. Every write is stamped with the user id in audit_log. The JSON endpoint uses a separate static API key in settings, not a session.
migration: 1) In Google Sheets, File > Download > CSV for each of the five sheets (or reuse the xlsx export already made) into /home/CPUSER/timeoff/import/. 2) bin/import_sheet.php --dry-run prints the plan: 15 employees, 177 time-off rows, 12 company events, 26 factory events, 5 sales events. Normalizations it applies: split 'Last, First' into two columns; lowercase type ('vacation' x4 fixed); ISO timestamps to DATE; titles trimmed; birthdays stored as month/day, and birth_year kept only when the year is before 2023 (so Walker J 1972, Fedak 2003, Kennedy 2006, Pirlot 2003 stay real; the 2023 and 2026 placeholders become NULL). 3) The importer also loads the sheet's stored columns E, F, G and the calculated allotments into tests/fixtures/sheet_2026-09-14.json and an import_verify table. 4) bin/verify.php (also /admin/selftest) recomputes every row with Balance.php and diffs: it must print '177/177 rows match, 0 mismatches' and a 15-line current/next balance table that must equal the known values (Walker R 2/3 14/15, Catuto 3/3 12/15, Ketter 2/3 10/15, Modzik 3/3 13/15, Swafford 1/3 15/15, Danalewich 3/3 15/15, Moss 3/3 0/5, Coleman 3/3 10/10, Walker J 2/3 0/5, six 2026 hires 0/0); with --compare-url it also fetches the old doGet JSON and diffs automatically. 5) Calendar adopt run: /admin/sync Dry run must show ~177 time-off, 30 birthday and 43 event adoptions with 0 creates and 0 deletes apart from the 5 retitled events; then run it live. 6) Run both systems side by side for one pay period: the sheet still drives the calendars, the app is used for entry and checked against it. 7) Cutover: in Apps Script delete the time-driven triggers, rename the sheet 'ARCHIVE - LSP Calendar Update' and protect all ranges, swap doGet to the proxy, enable sync in the app, send the office the URL with 'add to home screen' instructions.
deployment: File layout under /home/CPUSER/timeoff: public/ (index.php, .htaccess, assets/app.css, assets/app.js, manifest.webmanifest, icons/), src/ (Router, Db, Auth, Csrf, View, Balance, Google/ServiceAccount, Google/CalendarClient, Sync/CalendarSync, Controllers/*, Repo/* for employees, time_off, events, adjustments, audit), templates/*.php, migrations/001_init.sql ..., bin/ (migrate.php, sync.php, backup.php, import_sheet.php, verify.php), tests/fixtures/, config/ (config.php and google-sa.json, both gitignored), storage/ (logs, cache, backups; not web-readable), .cpanel.yml. Routes: /login, /logout, / (who's out), /time-off/new, /time-off/{id}/edit, /balances, /employees, /employees/new, /employees/{id}, /employees/{id}/edit, /calendar?m=2026-09, /events/{company|factory|sales}, /adjustments/new?employee=ID, /me, /admin/settings, /admin/sync, /admin/users, /admin/audit, /admin/selftest, /admin/upgrade, /api/preview, /api/balances.json. Cron (cPanel > Cron Jobs): '*/15 * * * * /opt/cpanel/ea-php82/root/usr/bin/php /home/CPUSER/timeoff/bin/sync.php >> /home/CPUSER/timeoff/storage/logs/sync.log 2>&1'; '10 2 * * * ... bin/sync.php --full'; '30 2 * * * ... bin/backup.php' (mysqldump via shell_exec, pure-PHP dump fallback, gzip to storage/backups/timeoff-YYYYMMDD.sql.gz, keep 30 days, plus Liquid Web's own account backups; Settings has a Download backup button). Update procedure: develop and test on XAMPP, commit, push to GitHub; in cPanel > Git Version Control click Pull or Deploy (the .cpanel.yml copies the tree into place); open /admin/upgrade, which applies any new migrations/*.sql in order inside a transaction and prints the result; check /admin/selftest is green. Zip upload via File Manager is the no-git fallback. Rollback: deploy the previous tag and restore last night's dump from phpMyAdmin.
risks: Strict-mirror sync deleting the wrong events if a calendar ID is mistyped or the service account is shared on the wrong calendar; mitigated by dry run, the 25-event / 20% delete guard, the adopt-first run, and per-calendar sync toggles.

Google Workspace admin may block service-account sharing or the calendars may be owned by a personal account; check who owns the five calendars before building the sync (day 4), and keep the ICS feed as the fallback.
Server PHP version below 8.1 or a missing extension; the /admin/health page checks this on day one, before any data is moved.
PHP mail() invites landing in spam; the admin set-temporary-password button is the fallback.
Date and timezone drift (DST, server clock in UTC); all dates are DATE columns and Y-m-d strings, timezone fixed to America/New_York in config, and the golden fixture catches regressions.
Feb 29 hire dates and zero-working-day ranges are edge cases; they are matched to the script's behaviour and covered by explicit test rows.
Cron path differences (/usr/local/bin/php may be a different version than the web PHP); use the ea-php82 binary path explicitly.
MySQL strict sql_mode differs between XAMPP and Liquid Web; migrations are tested on both and use explicit NOT NULL defaults.
An unknown consumer of the old doGet JSON URL; the Apps Script proxy keeps it alive and the new endpoint logs its callers so the consumer can be identified.
Single maintainer (bus factor 1); no framework, a README with the cPanel steps, and the fixture-based self-test keep the app understandable to any PHP contractor.
The four lowercase 'vacation' titles and one trailing-space factory title get rewritten on first sync, a harmless but visible change for staff subscribed to those calendars.
Departed-employee behaviour is new (history preserved, future events removed); confirm with the office manager that this is the wanted policy before cutover.
effort: About 6 focused working days (roughly 45 hours) for one PHP developer, in this order: Day 1 schema, migrations, Balance.php, importer and verify.php green against all 177 rows and the 15 known balances. Day 2 auth, employees, Add Time Off with live preview, Balances and employee ledger. Day 3 Who's Out, Office Calendar, Events, Adjustments, mobile polish and PWA manifest. Day 4 service-account client, mirror table, sync with dry run and adopt run, cron. Day 5 cPanel setup, deploy, side-by-side run and cutover checklist. Day 6 slack for surprises, audit and history screen, backups, README. First usable milestone is the end of Day 2: the app is live on the subdomain, Chris and the office manager can add employees and time off and see balances that verifiably match the sheet, while the sheet still drives the calendars; nothing is at risk until the sync is switched on in Day 4-5.

title: LSP Time Off: correctness-first PHP 8.2 / MySQL replacement for the "LSP Calendar Update" sheet on Liquid Web cPanel
lens: CORRECTNESS-AND-RISK-FIRST: balances are payroll data. Every choice below is ranked by (1) exact fidelity with the Apps Script rules, proven by a golden test against all 177 stored balances and the 15 current-cycle balances; (2) auditability (who changed what, when, with before/after values; no hard deletes anywhere in the app); (3) a calendar sync that keeps a ledger of the events it owns, never deletes anything it did not create, refuses mass deletions, and degrades gracefully when Google is unreachable; (4) migration behind a verification gate that refuses to commit on any mismatch; (5) backups Chris can restore alone. Only then is the stack chosen, and it is chosen to make those guarantees easiest on a stock cPanel account with no SSH, Composer, Node or Docker assumed.
stack:
LANGUAGE/RUNTIME: PHP 8.2 selected in cPanel MultiPHP Manager (EasyApache 4 package ea-php82; ea-php83 is fine if offered). Required extensions are all in the default EA4 profile: pdo_mysql, openssl (RS256-signs the Google service-account JWT), curl (Google REST), mbstring, json, ctype. Cron uses the pinned CLI binary /opt/cpanel/ea-php82/root/usr/bin/php so cron and web run the same PHP.

FRAMEWORK: none. A ~400-line micro-kernel Chris fully owns: public/index.php front controller; app/Kernel/Router.php (regex route table); app/Kernel/Db.php (PDO wrapper: ERRMODE_EXCEPTION, prepared statements only, transaction helper); app/Kernel/View.php (plain PHP templates with an e() escaping helper); app/Kernel/Auth.php; app/Kernel/Csrf.php; app/Kernel/Audit.php. A hand-written spl_autoload_register maps the App namespace onto app/. Why no Laravel/Slim: they need composer install plus a 20-40 MB vendor tree uploaded through File Manager and kept in step with the PHP version; the app is ~14 screens and the correctness guarantees live in two pure classes (BalanceEngine, CalendarSync) that a framework does not help with. The one thing Composer would buy is google/apiclient (30 MB); the subset needed (JWT bearer token + 5 REST calls) is ~150 lines of curl and is written by hand. Revisit only if the app grows well beyond this scope.

DATABASE: the MySQL 8 / MariaDB 10.6+ that cPanel provisions (Liquid Web ships one or the other; both work). InnoDB, utf8mb4, sql_mode STRICT_TRANS_TABLES enforced by the app on connect (SET SESSION sql_mode). All dates are DATE columns (no times, so no DST or timezone ambiguity). Every write is wrapped in a transaction that also inserts the audit_log row, so an audit row and its data change cannot be separated.

FRONT-END: server-rendered HTML forms. One vendored classless stylesheet (Pico CSS 2.x, ~80 KB, stored at public/assets/pico.min.css, no CDN so the app is unaffected by CDN outages or office content filters) and ~250 lines of vanilla JS (public/assets/app.js) for the live working-day / resulting-balance preview (fetch to /api/preview), overlap warnings and confirm dialogs. Native input type=date. No build step, no Node. Mobile-friendly out of the box.

GOOGLE CALENDAR: REST v3 over curl with a service account (JWT signed via openssl_sign, exchanged at oauth2.googleapis.com/token). Scope limited to https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.events (least privilege: cannot alter calendar sharing or delete calendars).

TESTS: bin/test.php, a tiny hand-rolled runner (assertSame/assertEquals) because PHPUnit needs Composer. Golden fixtures exported from the sheet live in tests/fixtures/.

LOCAL DEV: XAMPP (PHP 8.2 + MariaDB) with config/config.local.php; identical code to production, so what passes locally is what is uploaded.
hosting_fit:
Everything below is done in the cPanel UI or the Google web consoles; nothing needs SSH.

1. PHP version: cPanel > MultiPHP Manager > select the subdomain > ea-php82 (or ea-php83). Then MultiPHP INI Editor (basic mode) for the subdomain: memory_limit 256M, max_execution_time 120, upload_max_filesize 16M, date.timezone America/New_York, session.cookie_secure On, session.cookie_httponly On. The installer page (step 6) shows a red/green checklist of the required extensions (pdo_mysql, openssl, curl, mbstring, json) and the server's sql_mode and timezone, so any gap is visible before data is loaded.

2. Subdomain: cPanel > Domains > Create a New Domain: pto.lightsaberpromotions.com, UNCHECK "share document root", set Document Root to /home/USERNAME/lsp-pto/public. If DNS for lightsaberpromotions.com is on the same server the A record is created automatically; otherwise add an A record at the DNS host pointing to the server IP. AutoSSL issues the Let's Encrypt certificate within an hour of DNS resolving (cPanel > SSL/TLS Status > Run AutoSSL to force it). public/.htaccess redirects http to https and rewrites everything to index.php.

3. Database: cPanel > MySQL Database Wizard: database USERNAME_lsppto, user USERNAME_lsppto with a 32-char generated password, ALL PRIVILEGES (cPanel offers nothing finer-grained; the app never issues DDL at runtime except through bin/migrate.php or the admin "Apply database updates" button).

4. Files: cPanel > File Manager: upload lsp-pto-v1.0.0.zip to /home/USERNAME and Extract, producing /home/USERNAME/lsp-pto/ (app code lives OUTSIDE public_html; only lsp-pto/public is web-served). Copy config/config.example.php to config/config.php and fill DB name/user/password, APP_KEY (64 random hex chars, used for CSRF and token hashing), BASE_URL, ALERT_EMAIL (chris@lightsaberpromotions.com). Set config/ files to permission 600 via File Manager > Permissions. Also create config/my.cnf ([client] user/password/host) with 600 for mysqldump.

5. Google Cloud (one-time, ~20 minutes, done as Chris's Workspace account): console.cloud.google.com > New project "LSP PTO Sync" > APIs & Services > Enable "Google Calendar API" > IAM & Admin > Service Accounts > Create "lsp-pto-sync" > Keys > Add key (JSON) > download. Upload the JSON via File Manager to /home/USERNAME/lsp-pto/config/google-sa.json, permission 600. Then in Google Calendar (calendar.google.com, as the calendar owner) for EACH of the five calendars: Settings and sharing > Share with specific people > add lsp-pto-sync@lsp-pto-sync.iam.gserviceaccount.com with "Make changes to events". If Workspace blocks external sharing of secondary calendars, Admin console > Apps > Google Workspace > Calendar > Sharing settings > "External sharing options for secondary calendars" must allow "Share all information, and outsiders can change calendars" (the service account is technically external). If the admin cannot allow that, see calendar_sync for the OAuth fallback.

6. Install: browse to https://pto.lightsaberpromotions.com/install?key=APP_KEY. The installer runs db/migrations/*.sql, seeds the calendars table with the five calendar IDs from the Apps Script, creates the first admin user (Chris), runs the golden self-test on the fixture (must show 177/177), and then writes storage/installed.lock which disables the /install route permanently.

7. Cron: cPanel > Cron Jobs (see deployment for the exact four lines). Cron on cPanel runs as the account user with a normal shell, so mysqldump works from cron even if PHP disable_functions blocks exec from the web.

8. Settings page in the app: confirm the five calendar IDs, click "Test Google connection" (fetches each calendar's metadata with the service account and shows its name and the SA's access role, which must be "writer"), leave "Sync mode: dry run" ON until migration is signed off.

9. Nothing else on the server: no Composer, no Node, no Redis, no queue worker, no supervisor. The whole footprint is one directory, one database, four cron lines.
data_model:
All tables InnoDB, utf8mb4 (utf8mb4_unicode_ci on MariaDB, utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci on MySQL 8). Every mutable business table has created_by/created_at/updated_by/updated_at and soft delete (deleted_at/deleted_by/delete_reason). The app exposes no hard delete; "Delete" in the UI is a soft delete that requires a reason, and admins can Restore.

CREATE TABLE users (
  id INT UNSIGNED AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
  email VARCHAR(190) NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  display_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  password_hash VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  role ENUM('admin','editor','viewer') NOT NULL DEFAULT 'viewer',
  employee_id INT UNSIGNED NULL,            -- link so a viewer sees "my balance"
  is_active TINYINT(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  failed_logins TINYINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  locked_until DATETIME NULL,
  reset_token_hash CHAR(64) NULL, reset_expires DATETIME NULL,
  last_login_at DATETIME NULL,
  created_at DATETIME NOT NULL, updated_at DATETIME NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE employees (
  id INT UNSIGNED AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
  last_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
  first_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
  display_name VARCHAR(161) AS (CONCAT(last_name, ', ', first_name)) STORED,  -- reproduces the sheet's "Walker, Rebecca" exactly; used in calendar titles
  hire_date DATE NOT NULL,                  -- the anniversary anchor
  birth_month TINYINT UNSIGNED NULL, birth_day TINYINT UNSIGNED NULL,
  birth_year SMALLINT UNSIGNED NULL,        -- NULL for placeholder years; never shown as an age
  status ENUM('active','departed') NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active',
  separation_date DATE NULL,
  notes TEXT NULL,
  legacy_row INT UNSIGNED NULL,             -- sheet row at migration
  created_by INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL, created_at DATETIME NOT NULL,
  updated_by INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL, updated_at DATETIME NOT NULL,
  UNIQUE KEY uq_emp_name (last_name, first_name),
  CONSTRAINT ck_departed CHECK (status = 'active' OR separation_date IS NOT NULL)
);

CREATE TABLE time_off_requests (
  id INT UNSIGNED AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
  employee_id INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  kind ENUM('PTO','Vacation') NOT NULL,     -- canonical casing; the sheet's 'vacation' rows are normalized on import
  start_date DATE NOT NULL,
  end_date DATE NOT NULL,
  working_days TINYINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,   -- Mon-Fri inclusive, computed by BalanceEngine at save; nightly job re-verifies and alerts on drift
  note VARCHAR(255) NULL,
  legacy_row INT UNSIGNED NULL,
  created_by INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL, created_at DATETIME NOT NULL,
  updated_by INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL, updated_at DATETIME NOT NULL,
  deleted_at DATETIME NULL, deleted_by INT UNSIGNED NULL, delete_reason VARCHAR(255) NULL,
  CONSTRAINT fk_tor_emp FOREIGN KEY (employee_id) REFERENCES employees(id),
  CONSTRAINT ck_tor_range CHECK (end_date >= start_date),
  KEY ix_tor_emp_start (employee_id, start_date, id),
  KEY ix_tor_start (start_date)
);
-- Deliberately NO unique key on (employee, start, end): the sheet permits duplicates and a weekend-only row exists; the UI warns on overlap/zero working days but an editor may confirm, exactly as the sheet allowed.

CREATE TABLE balance_adjustments (                -- the never-created "PTO Adjustments" sheet, same semantics
  id INT UNSIGNED AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
  employee_id INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  kind ENUM('PTO','Vacation') NOT NULL,
  effective_date DATE NOT NULL,             -- selects the cycle: cycleStart <= effective_date < cycleEnd
  days DECIMAL(5,2) NOT NULL,               -- + grant, - deduction, fractional allowed (script allowed parseFloat)
