  reason VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,             -- mandatory: an adjustment without a reason is not auditable
  created_by INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL, created_at DATETIME NOT NULL,
  deleted_at DATETIME NULL, deleted_by INT UNSIGNED NULL, delete_reason VARCHAR(255) NULL,
  CONSTRAINT fk_adj_emp FOREIGN KEY (employee_id) REFERENCES employees(id),
  CONSTRAINT ck_adj_days CHECK (days <> 0),
  KEY ix_adj_emp_eff (employee_id, effective_date)
);

CREATE TABLE calendars (
  id TINYINT UNSIGNED PRIMARY KEY,
  slug VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL UNIQUE,         -- time_off, birthdays, additional_events, factory_closings, end_of_month_sale
  name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
  kind ENUM('time_off','birthdays','events') NOT NULL,
  google_calendar_id VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL, -- the five ...@group.calendar.google.com IDs from Code.gs, seeded by the installer
  sync_enabled TINYINT(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  accepts_new_events TINYINT(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,  -- 0 for end_of_month_sale (retired: history kept, hidden from entry forms)
  sort_order TINYINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
);

CREATE TABLE events (                             -- rows of the three [name, start, end] sheets
  id INT UNSIGNED AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
  calendar_id TINYINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  title VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
  start_date DATE NOT NULL, end_date DATE NOT NULL,
  note VARCHAR(255) NULL, legacy_row INT UNSIGNED NULL,
  created_by INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL, created_at DATETIME NOT NULL,
  updated_by INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL, updated_at DATETIME NOT NULL,
  deleted_at DATETIME NULL, deleted_by INT UNSIGNED NULL, delete_reason VARCHAR(255) NULL,
  CONSTRAINT fk_ev_cal FOREIGN KEY (calendar_id) REFERENCES calendars(id),
  CONSTRAINT ck_ev_range CHECK (end_date >= start_date),
  KEY ix_ev_cal_start (calendar_id, start_date)
);

CREATE TABLE calendar_links (                     -- the sync LEDGER: which Google event belongs to which row
  id INT UNSIGNED AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
  calendar_id TINYINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  source_type ENUM('request','event','birthday') NOT NULL,
  source_id INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,          -- time_off_requests.id / events.id / employees.id
  occurrence_year SMALLINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,   -- birthdays only (one link per year)
  google_event_id VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  fingerprint CHAR(40) NOT NULL,            -- sha1(title|start|end_exclusive) as last pushed
  state ENUM('synced','stale','delete_pending','deleted','error') NOT NULL,
  error_count TINYINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, last_error TEXT NULL,
  last_synced_at DATETIME NULL, created_at DATETIME NOT NULL, updated_at DATETIME NOT NULL,
  UNIQUE KEY uq_link_source (source_type, source_id, occurrence_year),
  UNIQUE KEY uq_link_gid (calendar_id, google_event_id)
);
-- Rows are never deleted; state='deleted' keeps the history of what was on the calendar and when it was removed.

CREATE TABLE sync_runs (
  id INT UNSIGNED AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
  started_at DATETIME NOT NULL, finished_at DATETIME NULL,
  trigger_kind ENUM('cron','manual','adopt') NOT NULL, dry_run TINYINT(1) NOT NULL,
  status ENUM('running','ok','partial','failed','aborted_guard') NOT NULL,
  created_n SMALLINT UNSIGNED DEFAULT 0, updated_n SMALLINT UNSIGNED DEFAULT 0, deleted_n SMALLINT UNSIGNED DEFAULT 0,
  unmanaged_n SMALLINT UNSIGNED DEFAULT 0, errors_n SMALLINT UNSIGNED DEFAULT 0,
  plan_json JSON NULL,                      -- the full plan (what would be created/updated/deleted) for review
  initiated_by INT UNSIGNED NULL
);

CREATE TABLE audit_log (                          -- append-only; the app has no code path that updates or deletes here
  id BIGINT UNSIGNED AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
  at DATETIME(3) NOT NULL,
  user_id INT UNSIGNED NULL, user_email VARCHAR(190) NULL, ip VARCHAR(45) NULL,
  action ENUM('insert','update','soft_delete','restore','login','login_failed','logout','sync','migrate','setting','import') NOT NULL,
  table_name VARCHAR(40) NULL, row_id INT UNSIGNED NULL,
  old_json JSON NULL, new_json JSON NULL,   -- full row before/after, so any change can be reversed by hand
  note VARCHAR(255) NULL,
  KEY ix_audit_row (table_name, row_id), KEY ix_audit_at (at), KEY ix_audit_user (user_id)
);

CREATE TABLE balance_snapshots (                  -- nightly record of what the engine said; makes silent drift visible
  id INT UNSIGNED AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
  snapshot_date DATE NOT NULL, employee_id INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  cycle_start DATE NOT NULL, cycle_end DATE NOT NULL, years_of_service TINYINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  pto_allot DECIMAL(5,2), pto_used DECIMAL(5,2), pto_remaining DECIMAL(5,2),
  vac_allot DECIMAL(5,2), vac_used DECIMAL(5,2), vac_remaining DECIMAL(5,2),
  engine_version VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
  UNIQUE KEY uq_snap (snapshot_date, employee_id, cycle_start)
);

CREATE TABLE settings (name VARCHAR(60) PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT NULL, updated_by INT UNSIGNED NULL, updated_at DATETIME NULL);
  -- keys: sync_mode (dry_run|live), api_token_hash, viewers_see_all_balances (0/1), alert_email, last_sync_ok_at, consecutive_sync_failures
CREATE TABLE schema_migrations (version VARCHAR(20) PRIMARY KEY, applied_at DATETIME NOT NULL);

HOW THE HARD CASES ARE HANDLED
- Employee departure: status='departed' + separation_date (required). Nothing is deleted: all requests, adjustments, links and audit rows stay; balances still compute for historical cycles; the Balances screen hides departed staff behind a toggle; new requests starting after separation_date are refused (existing ones get a warning badge); the birthday calendar stops generating their birthdays (the ledger removes only those birthday events); their time-off calendar events are left in place as history.
- Adjustments: balance_adjustments with the exact sumAdjustments semantics (effective_date in [cycleStart, cycleEnd) added to that cycle's allotment), fractional days allowed, mandatory reason.
- Event calendars: events rows keyed by calendars.id; end_of_month_sale is retired (accepts_new_events=0) but its 5 rows and calendar events are retained.
- Birthdays: month/day always; year NULL when the sheet held a placeholder (rule at import: year >= 2023 is a placeholder, which nulls the eight 2023 rows and the three 2026 rows and keeps 1972/2003/2006/2003). Birth year is never rendered as an age; it exists only so Chris can record it when known.
- Audit history: every insert/update/soft delete/restore writes old_json and new_json in the same transaction; logins, failed logins, sync runs, migrations and settings changes are audited too. The Audit screen filters by employee, table, user and date. Migration import is audited as action='import' with the sheet row number in legacy_row.
screens: LOGIN (/login) — everyone. Email + password, lockout after 10 failures for 15 minutes, all attempts audited. No self-registration.

BALANCES DASHBOARD (/) — admin/editor see every active employee; viewers see their own row plus the 'Who is out' strip (setting viewers_see_all_balances can open it up). Columns: employee, hire date, current cycle (start to end), years of service, PTO left/allotment, Vacation left/allotment, next cycle preview (allotments and the 'After MM/DD/YYYY: N PTO / N Vac' note if requests already exist there), last change (from audit). 'As of' date is shown and can be overridden by admins to reproduce a past date. balance_engine:
WHERE: app/Domain/BalanceEngine.php, a pure class with no database access and no clock: it receives plain arrays (employee hire date, requests, adjustments) and an explicit asOf date, and returns arrays. It is the ONLY place allotments, cycles or working days are computed; the dashboard, employee detail, live preview, API, nightly snapshot and the migration verifier all call it. ENGINE_VERSION = '1.0.0-sheet' is stamped into balance_snapshots so any future rule change is a new version whose effect on every historical cycle is visible as a snapshot diff.

LINE-BY-LINE PORT OF Code.gs (function correspondence is documented in the class header):
- yearsOfServiceAt(asOf, hire) = asOf.year - hire.year, minus 1 if (asOf.month, asOf.day) < (hire.month, hire.day).
- vacationAllotment(yos) = 15 if yos >= 10, 10 if >= 5, 5 if >= 1, else 0. ptoAllotment(yos) = 3 if yos >= 1 else 0.
- anniversaryWindow(ref, hire): anniversaryThisYear = makeDate(ref.year, hire.month, hire.day); start = anniversaryThisYear <= ref ? it : makeDate(ref.year - 1, ...); end = makeDate(start.year + 1, hire.month, hire.day). makeDate uses DateTimeImmutable::setDate which rolls Feb 29 to Mar 1 in non-leap years exactly like JavaScript's new Date(y, m, d); this is unit-tested even though no current hire date is Feb 29.
- workingDays(start, end): loop over inclusive range counting ISO weekdays 1-5; holidays are NOT excluded; no half days.
- cycle membership: a request belongs to the window containing its START date only (a range straddling an anniversary is counted entirely in the first cycle, as the script does; the entry form warns but does not block, matching the sheet).
- adjustments: sum of days with effective_date in [start, end) per kind, added to that cycle's allotment.
- runningBalances(employee): requests ordered by start_date then id (id preserves sheet row order after migration, reproducing the script's idx tie-break); running totals reset whenever the cycle changes; remaining = allotment - used after each row; the 'After MM/DD/YYYY: N PTO / N Vac' note is attached only when the row's cycle start equals addYears(currentCycleStart(asOf), 1).
- cycleRemaining(employee, offset) reproduces computeCycleRemaining for the API (offset 0 = current, 1 = next).
- Negative balances are allowed (the sheet allows them); the UI flags them, the engine does not clamp.
- asOf defaults to today's date in America/New_York (set explicitly in bootstrap; never trusts the server default, which on a Liquid Web box may be Central).

DATE HANDLING: dates are Y-m-d strings from DATE columns turned into DateTimeImmutable at midnight UTC purely for arithmetic, so DST never shifts a day. No timestamps are stored for business dates.

HOW IT STAYS IDENTICAL TO THE SHEET
1. Golden fixture tests/fixtures/sheet_2026-09-14.json: the 15 employee rows and all 177 request rows with the sheet's stored E/F values, plus the 15 current-cycle balances from the brief. bin/test.php replays the fixture through BalanceEngine with asOf=2026-09-14 and must produce 177/177 row matches and 15/15 cycle matches (the same check the Python re-implementation passed today). This test runs in the installer, in /admin/verify, and nightly.
2. Edge tests: weekend-only request = 0 days; 6-working-day span; first-anniversary boundary (request on the anniversary date belongs to the new cycle because start <= ref); day before anniversary belongs to the old cycle; <1 year employees get 0/0; year-10 tier jump; Feb 29 hire; adjustments at cycleStart (included) and at cycleEnd (excluded); fractional adjustment; type casing.
3. Stored working_days on each request is recomputed nightly by bin/snapshot.php; any divergence is emailed and shown on /sync as an integrity error.
4. Nightly balance_snapshots: a change in any past cycle's remaining value between consecutive snapshots that is not explained by an audit entry that day is reported (this is what catches an accidental hire_date edit or a silent engine change).
5. The API returns the same keys as getDataAsJson so any unknown consumer keeps working.
6. Performance: 15 employees x ~200 rows is under 5 ms; computed on every request, never cached, so there is no stale-cache class of bug.
calendar_sync:
DECISION: keep all five existing Google Calendars, same calendar IDs, same event titles ('Last, First - PTO' / 'Last, First - Vacation', 'Last, First Birthday', event titles verbatim), same all-day semantics. Staff change nothing on their phones. The database is the single source of truth and Google Calendar is a strictly read-only mirror; edits made in Google to a managed event are overwritten on the next sync and the /sync page says so. The 'Who is out' screen and an optional ICS feed (/feed/time_off.ics?token=) provide a fallback everyone can see from a phone if Google auth ever breaks, but they are a supplement, not a replacement.

AUTHENTICATION: Google service account (config/google-sa.json, chmod 600, outside the web root). app/Google/ServiceAccount.php builds a JWT {iss: SA email, scope: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.events, aud: https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token, iat, exp: +3600}, signs it with openssl_sign RS256 using the key in the JSON, POSTs grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer, and caches the access token in storage/cache/google_token.json (600) until 5 minutes before expiry. No user login, no refresh token that can be revoked by a password change, no consent screen that expires. FALLBACK if Workspace policy forbids sharing secondary calendars with an external service account: OAuth 2.0 'Internal' app type in the same Cloud project (internal apps have no 7-day refresh-token expiry), one-time consent by Chris from /settings, refresh token stored encrypted with APP_KEY in settings; the CalendarClient interface is identical so nothing else changes.

WHY NOT PORT THE EXISTING ALGORITHM: reading Code.gs shows (a) the delete pass compares the sheet's inclusive end date to getEndTime(), which for all-day events is the exclusive next-day midnight, so no event ever matches and every run deletes and recreates the entire PTO and event calendars (a crash mid-run leaves a half-empty calendar; event IDs never survive a run); (b) the create pass locates 'existing' events with a fuzzy search and then renames whatever it finds, so two employees off on the same dates can clobber each other (69 such overlapping same-type pairs exist in the data). Both are exactly the failure modes a payroll-grade mirror must not have.

DESIGN: ledger-based, per-item, idempotent. app/Sync/CalendarSync.php runs per calendar:
1. Desired state from the DB: time_off = every non-deleted request (departed employees included, history stays) as {key: request:ID, title: 'Last, First - Kind', start: start_date, end: end_date + 1 day}; birthdays = for every ACTIVE employee with a month/day, years {Y, Y+1} as {key: birthday:ID:Y, title: 'Last, First Birthday', description 'Birthday'} (Feb 29 rolls to Mar 1 like the script); events = every non-deleted events row for that calendar.
2. Plan: for each desired item look up calendar_links by (source_type, source_id, occurrence_year). No link -> CREATE. Link with fingerprint != desired fingerprint -> PATCH. Link whose source is gone (soft-deleted request/event, departed employee's birthday, past-year birthday no longer in {Y, Y+1}) -> DELETE. Every Google event we create carries extendedProperties.private.lsp_key = 'request:123' so the link can be rebuilt from Google alone if the ledger were ever lost (the list call can filter on privateExtendedProperty).
3. Guards, evaluated on the plan before any call is made: abort the run (status aborted_guard, email alert) if the desired set for time_off or birthdays is empty; refuse the delete portion if planned deletes exceed max(5, 10% of the ledger) unless an admin ticked 'I reviewed this plan' on /sync for that specific plan hash; refuse everything if sync_mode is dry_run (plan is stored in sync_runs.plan_json for review).
4. Execute: creates then patches then deletes, each API call immediately reflected in calendar_links (google_event_id, fingerprint, state, last_synced_at) inside its own small transaction, so a crash at any point resumes cleanly on the next run. 404 on PATCH means someone deleted the event in Google: recreate it. 404 on DELETE: mark deleted. 403 rateLimitExceeded / 5xx: retry with 1,2,4,8,16 s backoff, then mark the link error with error_count++ and continue with the rest (run status partial). Links with error_count >= 5 stop retrying and are listed on /sync for a human.
5. Reconcile: list every event on the calendar (singleEvents=true, timeMin 2021-01-01, maxResults 2500). Any event whose ID is not in the ledger is recorded as UNMANAGED (count in sync_runs.unmanaged_n, list on /sync). Unmanaged events are NEVER deleted automatically; an admin can adopt one (link it to a row) or tick it for explicit deletion. This is the guarantee that the app cannot silently delete calendar history. Managed events whose remote title/dates differ from desired are re-patched (fixes manual edits in Google).
6. Duplicates cannot arise: one link per source key (unique index), creates only happen when no link exists, and an insert whose response is lost is recovered on the next run by the privateExtendedProperty lookup before creating again.

FIRST-RUN ADOPTION (migration): with sync_mode = dry_run, 'Adopt existing events' lists each calendar's events and links each desired item to the remote event with an exact title and exact start/end match (the current script recreates everything each run, so exact matches are expected for everything the sheet knows about). Result report: adopted N, missing-in-Google M (will be created), unmanaged-in-Google K (listed; these are exactly the leftovers/clobbered events from the old fuzzy-search bug, to review by hand). Nothing is deleted in adopt mode. The birthday calendar adopts by title + date as well; prior-year birthday events show up as unmanaged and Chris decides.

CUTOVER ORDER (critical): (1) adopt pass and review while the Apps Script is still live; (2) in the Apps Script editor, Triggers: disable/delete every time-driven trigger and the onEdit/menu functions that call updateCalendarAndPTO, addBirthdaysToCalendar, updateAdditionalEvents, updateCalendarFactoryClosings, updateCalendarOtherEvents; (3) only then switch sync_mode to live. If both systems run at once the old script's delete-everything pass will wipe every event the new app creates within one trigger interval.

SCHEDULE AND TRIGGERS: cron every 15 minutes runs bin/sync.php under a flock on storage/locks/sync.lock (no overlapping runs). Saving a request/event/employee marks the affected link stale and sets settings.sync_requested; 'Save and sync now' runs the sync inline in the web request (typical run < 5 s for ~250 events, 60 s hard limit) and falls back to the flag if the lock is held. Total API volume is trivial (well under Google's 10k/day default quota even on the first full create).

FAILURE BEHAVIOR WHEN GOOGLE IS UNREACHABLE: data entry is never blocked; the request is saved, the balance is correct immediately, the link stays stale. The run is logged failed, consecutive_sync_failures increments, and after 3 consecutive failures (45 min) one alert email goes to ALERT_EMAIL via PHP mail() (repeated at most daily). A site-wide banner shows 'Calendars last synced N hours ago' once the last success is older than 2 hours. When Google returns, the next run drains everything pending. The 'Who is out' page and the ICS feed keep showing the truth from the database throughout.
auth:
WHO: named users in the users table; no self-registration. Roles: admin (Chris: everything, including users, settings, sync live mode, adjustments, restores, migrate, backup); editor (whoever enters time off day to day: employees, requests, company events; cannot touch users/settings/adjustments or run deletes on Google); viewer (staff who want to see their own balance and who is out; can be linked to their employee row; setting viewers_see_all_balances=1 opens the full dashboard if the office prefers that). Viewer accounts are optional: the five shared calendars remain the primary way staff see time off.

PASSWORDS: password_hash with PASSWORD_ARGON2ID where the build supports it, otherwise bcrypt cost 12; minimum 12 characters; no complexity theatre. Lockout: 10 failed attempts locks the account 15 minutes (failed_logins/locked_until), every attempt audited with IP. Password reset without an email dependency: an admin generates a one-time link (32-byte token stored hashed, 24 h expiry) and hands it over in person; optionally mail() it. Optional later: Google Sign-In restricted to the lightsaberpromotions.com domain, since everyone already has Workspace accounts; not in v1 to keep setup minimal.

SESSIONS: PHP native sessions with session.save_path = /home/USERNAME/lsp-pto/storage/sessions (not the shared /tmp on a shared server), cookie flags Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, session_regenerate_id on login and on privilege change, idle timeout 12 hours, absolute lifetime 14 days, logout destroys the session. HTTPS enforced by .htaccess redirect plus Strict-Transport-Security; AutoSSL keeps the certificate renewed. CSRF: a per-session token embedded in every form and checked on every POST, with SameSite=Lax as the second layer. Security headers set in bootstrap: Content-Security-Policy default-src 'self', X-Frame-Options DENY, Referrer-Policy same-origin (no external assets, so a strict CSP is painless).

API TOKEN: /api/balances.json accepts Authorization: Bearer <token> or ?token= for URL-only consumers; the token is 32 random bytes shown once and stored as a SHA-256 hash in settings; regenerating it is audited. Rate-limited to 60 requests/min per IP (file-based counter). The Apps Script doGet can be left deployed as a one-line proxy (UrlFetchApp to the new endpoint with the token in Script Properties) so the old URL keeps working for any consumer that turns up.

SECRETS ON DISK: config/config.php, config/google-sa.json, config/my.cnf all live outside the document root with mode 600; the web root contains only index.php, .htaccess and static assets. The service account can only edit events on calendars explicitly shared with it and cannot read anything else in Workspace.
migration:
SOURCE OF TRUTH FOR THE MOVE: a fresh File > Download > .xlsx of the sheet taken on cutover day (the dump analysed today is the dress rehearsal). bin/import_sheet.php reads the workbook via a tiny built-in XLSX reader (ZipArchive + SimpleXML, both standard in PHP) or, if Chris prefers, the five sheets saved as CSV.

STEPS (all repeatable; the importer refuses to run twice against a non-empty database unless --wipe-staging is given, and everything happens in one transaction that is rolled back on any failure):
1. Employees (15): split 'Last, First' on the first comma/space into last_name/first_name and assert that CONCAT(last_name, ', ', first_name) equals the original string byte-for-byte (this is what keeps calendar titles identical); hire_date from column B; birthday month/day from column C, birth_year set to NULL when the year is >= 2023 (placeholders: eight 2023 rows, three 2026 rows) and kept otherwise (1972, 2003, 2006, 2003); legacy_row recorded; created_by = the migration user; audit action import.
2. Requests (177): trim names and resolve to employee_id (unknown name = hard failure, none expected); type normalized to PTO/Vacation (the four 'vacation' rows); start/end as DATE; working_days computed by BalanceEngine; rows inserted in sheet row order so id order reproduces the script's tie-break; the sheet's stored E/F values and the sheet row number are kept in a staging table for verification. The Danalewich 2026-05-16 weekend-only row is imported as-is (0 working days) and flagged in the report for Chris to decide later; it is not silently dropped.
3. Events: 12 Additional Events, 26 Factory Closings (including the 2023 party/luncheon/sale rows that live on that sheet; they are imported where they are and listed in the report as 'possibly misfiled', not moved), 5 End Of Month Sale rows into the retired calendar.
4. Adjustments: none exist; the table starts empty.
5. VERIFICATION GATE (still inside the transaction): (a) BalanceEngine running balances for every imported request must equal the sheet's E/F for all 177 rows; (b) current-cycle balances with asOf = cutover date must equal the values printed by the same Python script run on the same export that morning (Walker R 2/3 14/15, Catuto 3/3 12/15, Ketter 2/3 10/15, Modzik 3/3 13/15, Swafford 1/3 15/15, Danalewich 3/3 15/15, Moss 3/3 0/5, Coleman 3/3 10/10, Walker J 2/3 0/5, six 2026 hires 0/0 as of 2026-09-14); (c) row counts per employee and per event sheet match; (d) allotment columns D/E on the employee sheet match vacationAllotment/ptoAllotment at asOf. Any mismatch prints a row-level diff and ROLLS BACK; nothing partial can land. On success the importer writes storage/migration-report-<date>.txt (counts, flags, the verification tables) and the audit_log gets one 'import' row per table with the report hash.
6. Calendar adoption: with sync in dry-run, run 'Adopt existing events' on /sync and review the report: adopted/missing/unmanaged per calendar (see calendar_sync). Missing items will be created on the first live run; unmanaged items are Chris's call.
7. Parallel run (1-2 weeks, recommended given the payroll nature): the sheet stays live and keeps driving the calendars; every new request is entered in BOTH places; each evening /admin/verify is run against a fresh export (drag-and-drop the .xlsx onto the page) and must show 0 mismatches. The API is compared to doGet output once.
8. Cutover checklist: final export and re-import into an empty database (or import only the rows added since, matched by legacy_row); verify gate green; Apps Script triggers disabled; sheet renamed 'ARCHIVE - LSP Calendar Update (read only)' with all ranges protected; sync_mode set to live; first live sync reviewed on /sync; two staff confirm their phones still show their calendars; the API token given to any doGet consumer found in Apps Script > Executions over the previous 90 days (if none, the endpoint is simply retired).
9. Rollback: until the sheet is un-protected and the triggers re-enabled nothing has changed for staff; the nightly .sql.gz and the archived sheet make either direction recoverable.

risks: Two writers on the same calendars during cutover: the Apps Script's sync is delete-everything-then-recreate, so if its triggers are still enabled when the new app goes live, every event the new app creates is wiped within one trigger interval and the new app then recreates them, ping-ponging forever. Mitigation: the cutover checklist disables triggers before sync_mode=live, the adopt pass runs in dry-run only, and the mass-deletion guard would halt the new side if the ledger suddenly emptied.

Workspace policy may forbid sharing secondary calendars with an external service account (the SA address is outside the domain). Mitigation: check the Admin console sharing setting on day one; fallback is an Internal OAuth app authorised once by Chris, with the same CalendarClient interface.

An unknown consumer of the Apps Script doGet endpoint may exist. Mitigation: check Apps Script > Executions for doGet calls over 90 days before cutover; keep the old URL alive as a proxy to the new API; keep JSON keys byte-compatible.

The old fuzzy-search sync may already have clobbered or duplicated events on the PTO calendar (69 cross-employee overlapping same-type requests). Mitigation: the adopt report lists every missing/unmanaged event; missing ones are recreated, unmanaged ones are reviewed by hand, nothing is auto-deleted.

Rules the sheet encodes that HR may not intend: holidays count as used days, weekend-only rows count 0, negative balances allowed, ranges straddling an anniversary land entirely in the first cycle, no carry-over. Mitigation: preserved exactly (fidelity first) with warnings in the entry form; any policy change is a new ENGINE_VERSION whose effect on every historical cycle is shown by the snapshot diff before it is enabled.

Editing a hire date silently re-cycles all of an employee's history. Mitigation: the edit form shows a before/after balance diff and requires confirmation; old/new values are in audit_log; nightly snapshot comparison flags any past-cycle change not matched by an audit entry.

cPanel server surprises: PHP 8.2 not offered, disable_functions blocking exec, no mysqldump on the cron PATH, sql_mode not strict, server timezone not New York. Mitigation: installer checklist page shows each of these; the app never needs exec; PDO-based dump fallback; timezone set in code and cron; only additive migrations.

Single maintainer (Chris) and a hand-rolled kernel: if he is away nobody else can fix it. Mitigation: no framework churn to keep up with, one config file, a README runbook with the update/restore/cron procedures, every rule in one 200-line engine file with the sheet correspondence documented, and the CSV export that can always put the data back into a spreadsheet.

Google outage or key revocation makes calendars stale. Mitigation: entry never blocks; stale links drain on recovery; banner after 2 h; email after 3 failures; the in-app Who is out page and optional ICS feed show the truth meanwhile.

Credential exposure on a shared host: DB password, SA key, API token. Mitigation: secrets outside the web root at mode 600, SA scope limited to calendar.events on five explicitly shared calendars, token stored hashed, HTTPS + HSTS + strict CSP, sessions in a private directory, argon2id/bcrypt passwords, lockout and audit of every login attempt.

Birthday placeholders: eight 2023 and three 2026 birth years are not real; displaying ages or sorting by year would embarrass someone. Mitigation: birth_year nulled on import, never rendered as an age, month/day is all the calendar needs.

Migration name-splitting or type-casing errors could attach a request to the wrong person. Mitigation: exact round-trip assertion on display_name, unknown names are fatal, the verification gate compares all 177 stored balances and per-employee counts, and the whole import rolls back on any mismatch.
Alert emails from shared hosting can land in spam. Mitigation: alerts are a secondary channel; the /sync page and site-wide banner are primary; cPanel cron mail on stderr is a third signal.

Date edge cases (Feb 29 hire or birthday, DST changes). Mitigation: DATE-only storage, UTC-midnight arithmetic, explicit unit tests reproducing JavaScript's Feb 29 to Mar 1 rollover so behaviour matches the script rather than differing silently.
